summary.name: Zotero
summary.one_liner: Zotero is a free, open source research tool that collects, organizes, cites, and shares references and documents.
use_cases: Collecting sources while browsing journals and news sites
Generating citations and bibliographies in a paper
Organizing research with collections and tags
Sharing course reading lists with students
Building a shared bibliography for a group
summary.what_it_does: Zotero detects research pages as you browse and saves items such as articles, preprints, news stories and library books. You can organize items into collections, tag them with keywords, and create saved searches that fill automatically. It creates in-text references and bibliographies inside Word, LibreOffice, and Google Docs, with support for over 9,000 citation styles. Optional sync keeps files, notes, and records up to date across devices and can be accessed from any web browser.
notable: Open source and run by a independent nonprofit
Automatic detection of research pages while browsing
Share libraries with unlimited people at no cost
caveats: Syncing across devices is optional and the page does not detail its storage limits
